definition: All parties fall within one of the following three categories: (1) proper parties; (2) necessary parties; and (3) indispensable parties. Proper parties are ones whose interest may be affected by a judgment, but whose presence is not essential in order for the court to adjudicate the rights of others. Proper parties may be added to a lawsuit through a permissive joinder. Example: In an action for negligence where two defendants are jointly and severally liable, each defendant is a proper party. The plaintiff has a right to sue either of the defendants, but only one of the defendants is required.
